newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador sugar harvest seen higher in 1996-1997.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador sugar harvest seen higher in 1996-1997.

text.p: El Salvador predicts sugar output in the upcoming 1996-1997 cycle will grow to 340,000 tonnes, up 20,000 tonnes on the 1995-1996 campaign, the manager of the the National Sugar Association said Monday.
Mario Salaverria told Reuters the boost in production will come because of an increase in the surface area under cultivation of 2,800 hectares to 52,000 hectares.
Salaverria said output in the last cycle was 320,000 tonnes of sugar and 155,000 tonnes of secondary molasses.

El Salvador's sugar crop starts toward the end of November and Salaverria said he expected 225,000 tonnes of sugar would be consumed by the domestic markets, leaving 115,000 tonnes for export. El Salvador has a 50,000 tonne export quota with the United States, he added.
